title: Open the Door, Damaad Ji
logline: Kiran gives Mausi the alarm, and the gang comes up the stairs to a door Aditya padlocked from the inside. Mausi, who meets no one, drives two and a half hours to stand at it herself. She reads his notebook and his photograph, knows whose hand is in the print and keeps quiet, and presses two sachets into Kiran's palm: this time the whole sachet, by her own hand.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; Mausi, beta, Damaad ji, lakh and party kept as they are said in India.
script_note: Indian English in Latin script. Hindi kinship terms and the trade word 'party' kept; no British or American colour.

characters.name: Kiran
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride, tonight 'Sneha'. She has just given Mausi the alarm.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Wheat-brown skin, oval face, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, a closed, watchful mouth. Low bun, centre parting with sindoor, small round red bindi, thin plain gold ring in the LEFT nostril, small gold studs, short black-bead mangalsutra. Plain sindoor-red matte saree with a 1 cm plain gold border, red elbow-sleeve blouse, pallu over the left shoulder, barefoot. Block henna on both hands (a solid disc in each palm, fingertips dipped). Red-and-ivory chooda on both forearms, each reading as a red cuff about 10 cm long with a pale band at each end; the LEFT cuff is complete and covers the scar in every shot of this episode.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge. Small-city Madhya Pradesh Indian English, learnt at school and from a phone: simple, quick, contractions, a light Hindi accent; not British, not American. The 'Sneha' voice is gone: lower, flat, quick and blunt with Aditya. With Mausi she sounds younger and keeps 'Mausi'. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill.

characters.name: Aditya
characters.role: The groom. A pharmacist who made himself the gang's mark to reach Mausi and the bride who robbed his brother.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow, slight stoop. Light-brown skin, long clean-shaven face, neat left-parted short black hair, rimless rectangular glasses in every shot. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta with band collar and three cloth buttons, sleeves folded back once, cream churidar, barefoot. A 5 cm brass key on a doubled red thread worn outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch with brown strap on the left wrist, never readable.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken. Careful small-city Madhya Pradesh Indian English, a science graduate's: complete sentences, precise nouns, no slang, an educated Hindi accent; not British, not American. Even and unhurried; under pressure he slows down and drops in volume. Never shouts.

characters.name: Shakun Mausi
characters.role: Runs the brides. A voice on Billu's phone and through the door until b9, where she is seen for the first time in the series.
characters.look: Indian woman, 56, about 5 ft 2, broad and heavy-shouldered. Brown skin, round face, heavy-lidded shrewd eyes, paan-reddened lips and a smile that arrives before she speaks, large round maroon bindi, small gold nose stud, grey-streaked hair oiled into a tight bun. Starched bottle-green cotton saree with a narrow mustard border, pallu pinned on the left shoulder, mustard elbow-sleeve blouse, thin gold chain, rubber slippers. A steel ring of about eight keys hooked at her LEFT hip. A dozen plain green glass bangles on each wrist.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, mid 50s, low, warm and grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Warm, motherly Indian English with a strong Bundelkhand-side Hindi accent, short plain sentences, like someone's aunt at a wedding; not British, not American. Keeps beta and Damaad ji. Never raises her voice: the colder the decision, the softer and slower. On the phone and through the door she is fully voiced and clear, never a whisper.

characters.name: Billu
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry and restless. Brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, black hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket, sleeves pushed up, over a black round-neck T-shirt, dark jeans, grey-white sneakers. A wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth (spat out in b2, a fresh one back in from b9). A car key on a plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger. No weapon.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, about 30, light tenor, fast, a little nasal, talks round a toothpick. Quick, slangy small-town Indian English with a heavy Bundelkhand Hindi accent, an article dropped now and then; keeps Mausi and 'party'. Never American street slang, not British. Surprised, he goes loud for one line, then looks to Mausi for the next move. To Mausi: quick and obedient.

characters.name: The boys
characters.look: Never a face. Two fixed shapes: one heavy-set with a shaved head and a maroon track jacket; one thin, in a checked shirt and a cloth cap. Only backs, hands, boots and backlit silhouettes, heads cropped, turned away or in full shadow.
characters.voice_note: No lines. Any breath or grunt is a sound effect.

location: The first-floor bridal bedroom of a rented house in a small Madhya Pradesh city, with its landing and the lane below. Bedroom: about 3 by 3.5 m, dark wood double bed with white sheet, red bolster, loose marigold petals and a marigold fringe above the headboard; pale-green lime-washed walls, no pictures. Facing the bed from its foot: window with iron grille in the RIGHT wall, grey-green steel almirah and a wooden chair against the LEFT wall, pale-blue double door BEHIND, with an iron bolt and hasp on the inside shut by a brass padlock. A low stool on the window side holds a steel tray with the untouched steel glass of kesar milk and the half-emptied paper fold. Landing: narrow concrete stairs, damp-stained cream walls, one bare yellow bulb. Lane: shuttered two-storey houses, Billu's old white sedan under one sodium streetlight, a motorbike behind it, nobody else.
time_of_day: Night 1 of late April, from 2:00 am (the end of the call) to about 4:35 am. Bedroom light: warm amber bedside lamp on the almirah side and cool streetlight through the grille; headlights on the ceiling at about 4:30; from b8 a line of yellow landing light at the door, and from b9 the landing bulb spilling in through the open door.

beats.action: Opens inside the in-breath that ended s1e02. Set-up 1 (l01, l02): close on Kiran's mouth and eyes, her phone lit and face up on the sheet between them, on speaker, where s1e02 b13 left it, her right hand flat beside it, her left arm under the fall of the pallu; out of focus beyond her, Aditya's glasses, the brass key on its red thread and the steel dabba still in his hand. Mausi's reply comes from the phone. Set-up 2 (the silence after): insert of the steel glass on the tray between them, the milk whole and smooth, no skin, nothing split; at the edge of frame Aditya's eyes have dropped to it. One second late, he understands that was not the answer to the check.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Mausi... the milk has split.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Don't worry, beta.

beats.action: The lane, one still. Billu by the white sedan under the sodium streetlight, face turned up to the lit first-floor window, the toothpick falling from his lips; behind him, by the motorbike, two backlit shapes straighten up, heads in shadow. The car door and boots on the road are sound only.

Bedroom. Boots on the stairs, as sound, getting closer under every line. Set-up 1 (l03, l05): Aditya on the bed, single, very still, key at his chest, glasses catching the lamp, the dabba set down on the sheet beside him. Set-up 2 (l04, l06): Kiran on the window side of the bed, single, the phone dark in her right hand, left arm under the pallu. They are a bed's width apart.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] What did you tell her?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] What I had to. Eighteen lakh, and my home.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] I had given you a way out.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sharply] My way out is coming up the stairs.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (l07): the landing, under the bare yellow bulb. Billu at the pale-blue door, fist raised from the one bang; behind him on the stairs, two backs, heads cropped. This side of the door shows no lock. Set-up 2 (l08, first half; bedroom plate): the reverse, inside the bedroom: Kiran at the door, her right palm flat on the wood, the brass padlock on the bolt beside her hand, left arm under the pallu; STATE: her phone left face down on the bed. Set-up 3 (l08, last clause; bedroom plate): Aditya on the bed, single, hand closed round the brass key; he has just heard her real name. The door rattles once against the hasp and holds.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [nervous] Kiran! You okay in there?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] I'm fine. The lock's on the inside. Key's round his neck.

beats.action: The landing. Set-up 1 (l09): Billu single, his back to the shut door, phone at his ear, the steel key ring on his finger. Set-up 2 (l10): from the landing down the stairs, the boys' backs under the bare yellow bulb, heads cropped, a maroon shoulder and a cloth cap; Mausi's voice over. Set-up 3 (l11): Billu close, listening, the key ring still on his finger. Mausi is a voice on the phone throughout. Set-up 4 (l12): Billu has lowered the phone and turned his mouth to the crack of the door, one hand flat on it.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [nervous] Mausi, the party's locked the door from inside.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] A man who locks the bride in is not a party.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Wait for me. Don't touch him.

lines.speaker: billu
lines.text: [sharply] Kiran! Mausi's coming herself. Two and a half hours.

beats.action: About 2:05, no overlay. Set-up 1 (l13, l29; about 8.5 s at measured rates: S7 holds it on its camera move): Aditya has stood up from the bed and taken a step towards her, single, looking down. Set-up 2 (l14): Kiran sitting on the floor with her back against the pale-blue door, knees up, her left arm folded under the pallu, her right hand on her knee; the padlock on the bolt above her shoulder. Set-up 3 (the silence after): the room from the window side, wide enough for both: Aditya sitting back down on the edge of the bed, Kiran against the door, a room's width between them. The landing creaks on the other side of the wood. This framing is the one b6 repeats.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] You said there was no code. Show me your hands.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] I told you, didn't I? It was a lie, so I will check the wrist myself.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Touch me and I'll scream. Then the boys outside will break down the door.

beats.action: Overlay: 4:10. Set-up 1 (the silence, then l15): the same wide framing as the end of b5a, unchanged: she has not left the door and he has not left the bed; his plain grey phone, taken from the right side pocket of his kurta together with a small black notebook, is now in his hand, the notebook held under it, the phone's screen turned away from camera, lighting his glasses. Set-up 2 (l16): insert, the brass padlock on the bolt above Kiran's shoulder, her head at the frame edge. Set-up 3 (l17): Kiran against the door, single. Set-up 4 (l18): Aditya single, the phone going face down on the sheet. Insert under the end of l18: on the white sheet beside him, the creased photograph and the small black notebook squared together, the phone face down beside them, nothing readable.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [sharply] Calling the police? What will you show them?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] You're the one who put the lock on. Even your name at the bureau is fake.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] And Mausi's just coming to fetch her daughter.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Fourteen months I searched. Now she comes to me.

beats.action: No line. Set-up 1 (about 2.5 s: engine, car door, car leaving): the ceiling above the bed, the marigold fringe, and a band of white headlight lying across the lime-wash; no person in frame. A car door below; the car is heard pulling away, it does not wait. Set-up 2 (about 3.0 s: the keys on the stairs): Kiran is up from the door and standing on the window side of the bed, her back near the grille, left arm under the pallu; Aditya on the bed, both faces turned to the door. Keys chinking, slowly, step by step, up the stairs. Kiran is clear of the door in both frames.

Set-up 1 (the crack): insert of the inside of the pale-blue door: the hasp's screws torn out of the old wood, the brass padlock hanging, still locked, from the bolt; a thin line of yellow landing light along the edge of the door. The door stays shut. Set-up 2 (l19): Kiran on the window side and Aditya by the bed, two-shot, both looking at the door. Mausi is a voice through it. Glimpse B ends on this line.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Open the door, Damaad ji.

beats.action: Aditya pulls the door open himself. Set-up 1 (the 2.0 s silence before l20, with the hinges and keys under it): Mausi's first image in the series: standing in the doorway with the landing bulb behind her, green saree, keys at her left hip, paan smile; only Aditya's hand on the door leaf is in frame; Billu and the boys are out of frame on the landing. Set-up 2 (l20): two-shot, Mausi and Kiran by the lamp: Mausi has turned Kiran's face to the light with one hand and holds both Kiran's hands in the other, palms up, looking for marks; palms up, both cuffs whole, nothing on the outer forearm shows. Kiran meets Mausi's eyes, steady; Mausi's turn to the namaste in set-up 3 is the answer. Set-up 3 (l21, first sentence 'नमस्ते, दामाद जी।'): Mausi single, palms joined in a namaste towards Aditya. Set-up 4 (l21, second and third sentences 'दरवाज़े का बुरा मत मानिए। कुंडी तोड़नी पड़ी।'): insert, Aditya seated on the wooden chair by the almirah (Kiran's maroon bag now on the floor beside it), two pairs of hands on his shoulders, the bodies cropped at the neck.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Look at me, beta. Did he touch you?

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Namaste, Damaad ji. Please don't mind the door. We had to break the latch.

beats.action: Silence split: 3.0 s before l22 (set-ups 1 to 3, about 1.0 s each) and a 0.8 s hold after l23 (end of set-up 7), 3.8 s in all. Set-up 1 (silent): Billu single, a fresh toothpick in, sliding Aditya's grey phone from the sheet into his jacket pocket. Set-up 2 (silent): Mausi on the edge of the bed, single, the small black notebook open in her lap, pages angled away and unreadable. Set-up 3 (silent): insert, the creased photograph between her green-bangled fingers, the one print image used throughout the series. Set-up 4 (l22, 'तो ये मोहित का भाई है।'): Mausi single, eyes lifting from the print. Set-up 5 (l22, 'हाँ, ख़बर आई थी।'): insert, Kiran's left forearm at her side, the red cuff whole, the pallu edge over it; this is where Mausi's look lands, the near miss. Set-up 6 (l22, 'लड़का कमज़ोर निकला।'): back to Mausi single. She says nothing about whose hand it is. Set-up 7 (l23, l30 and the 0.8 s hold after them; about 7 s at measured rates): Kiran single. Mausi does not answer; behind Kiran, out of focus, Aditya on the chair with the hands on his shoulders.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] So this is Mohit's brother. Yes, I heard. The boy turned out weak.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [hesitant] You knew Mohit was dead, Mausi?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] And you never told any of us?

beats.action: Mausi, practical. Set-up 1 (l24, l25): Mausi single on the bed, closing the notebook on the photograph and tapping it once. Set-up 2 (l26): Aditya single on the wooden chair, the hands on his shoulders, glasses and key in the lamp; Billu's shoulder at the frame edge. Set-up 3 (l27): Kiran single, standing, left arm under the pallu, the untouched steel glass on its tray soft beyond her. Set-up 4 (l28, first sentence 'इस बार पूरी पुड़िया, बेटा।'): two-shot, Mausi taking Kiran's LEFT hand, palm up, the cuff whole at the wrist, two small white paper folds already between Mausi's fingers, brought from the tuck of her saree at the waist. Set-up 5 (l28, 'अपने हाथ से।'): insert, the two folds pressed onto the henna disc in Kiran's left palm, Mausi's green-bangled fingers closing Kiran's over them; beyond, soft, the untouched steel glass on its tray. Cut on the last word.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] This one won't get scared, beta.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [chuckles] Fourteen months he's kept accounts.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] So they'll all say: the bride ran off, the groom never woke up.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [quietly] One brother died of shame. Who'll ask about the other?

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] This time the whole sachet, beta. With your own hands.

sfx_notes: Bed, bedroom, loopable: still late-April night room tone, crickets and a far dog through the open grille, the lamp's faint hum. No ceiling fan anywhere in the room or the mix.

b1: l02 through the phone speaker in the room: narrow band but wide enough that every consonant survives. After l02, call-ended tones, three short beeps. Duck the bed under l01: it is the locked line, one whole take, no cut-off.
b2: a wooden toothpick ticking on tarmac; the car door; a motorbike side-stand kicked up; two pairs of boots on the road.
b3: boots on narrow concrete stairs, rising in level under l03 to l06 and stopping at the landing just after l06.
b4: one fist bang on a wooden double door. l07 is played loud through the door: on the bedroom side it is muffled but clear. After l08 the door rattles once against the hasp and holds.
b5: landing acoustic, small and hard. Mausi on Billu's phone, filtered as in b1, fully voiced. l12 is Billu calling through the door crack, loud and close.
b5a: after l14, one creak of a foot shifting on the landing, then Aditya's weight on the bed.
b6: the time cut is carried by the overlay, not by sound: the bed continues unchanged. The phone set face down on the sheet: a soft tap.
b7: an engine approaching down the lane and idling; one car door; the car pulling away. Then keys chinking, slowly, one step at a time, up the stairs. No music under the keys.

b8: one dry crack of screws tearing out of old wood; the padlock swinging and knocking twice against the door; a breath of silence. l19 comes through the shut door, lightly muffled, fully voiced, warm and clear; the bed ducks under it.
b9: door hinges and keys chinking at Mausi's hip under the 2.0 s silence before l20; green glass bangles; a wooden chair scraping as the boys seat Aditya under the second sentence of l21.
b10: the zip of Billu's jacket pocket at the head of the silence; a notebook page turning; the flick of the print. After l30, 0.8 s of room tone with no answer.
b11: paper folds crinkling into a palm; glass bangles. Bed and music duck right down under l28 so every word is clear. Cut to silence on its last word, 0.5 s of room tone.
music_note: No music in b1: the call and the breath only. A low sustained drone enters with the boots in b3 and sits under b4 and b5. It drops out for b5a and the time cut, and does not return in b7: engine and keys alone. One slow sub pulse from the crack in b8, held low under Mausi's scenes. Drone and pulse duck under l19 and l28 and cut dead with the picture at the end.
ending_question: Will Kiran really pour the whole sachet into Aditya's milk with her own hands?
writer_notes: English adaptation (S5) of script.hi.json, not a literal translation. Same beats, speakers, line ids (l01 to l30; l29 sits after l13 in b5a and l30 after l23 in b10, as in the Hindi) and order, and the same silent_seconds and silent_position per beat, so both cuts share one set of frames. Only text, emotion_tags and target_seconds differ in the lines, plus supers[].text. Sources: content/series1/bible.json (voice_note_en and the English sample lines per character, the English title) and docs/decisions.md D-003 direction 7, D-005, D-007 directions 1 and 5 to 7, D-013, D-014 and D-024.

action, on_screen, location, sfx_notes and music_note are the same as the Hindi script, byte for byte, including the Hindi sentences quoted in the action text (the D-024 pass changed the action in b5a set-up 1, b9 set-up 4 and b10 set-ups 4 and 7, and sfx b10 now reads 'After l30'; all copied here). English sentence mapping for those set-ups: b5a set-up 1 is l13 then l29; b9 set-up 3 is 'Namaste, Damaad ji.' and set-up 4 is 'Please don't mind the door. We had to break the latch.'; b10 set-up 4 is 'So this is Mohit's brother.', set-up 5 (the forearm insert, the near miss) is 'Yes, I heard.', set-up 6 is 'The boy turned out weak.', set-up 7 is l23 and l30; b11 set-up 4 is 'This time the whole sachet, beta.' and set-up 5 is 'With your own hands.'.

Locked lines in English: l01 'Mausi... the milk has split.' is the bible's English code phrase and D-003 direction 7's (a mother's check-in, not an alarm); one whole take. l19 'Open the door, Damaad ji.' is the bible's English line and the English episode title. l03 'What did you tell her?' is the plain English of the locked Hindi line. All three are unchanged by the D-024 pass.

Register: Kiran simple and quick with contractions; Aditya in complete, careful sentences (l05 'I had given you a way out.' uses the Indian English past perfect on purpose; l29 'I will check the wrist myself' keeps his uncontracted 'I will'); Mausi in short plain sentences with beta and Damaad ji kept; Billu quick, keeps 'party' as the trade's word for the mark. 'Eighteen lakh' is kept, not converted. l15 'Calling the police? What will you show them?' keeps the taunt and sets up l16 and l17 as the answer. l16 'You're the one who put the lock on' carries the stress the Hindi word order puts on तुमने; 'Even your name at the bureau is fake' is the भी of 'Bureau में नाम भी तुम्हारा नकली है'.

Meaning checks: l17 is 'to fetch her daughter', not 'coming for her daughter', which in English sounds like a threat and would undo Kiran's argument that Mausi looks innocent. l26 'So tomorrow they'll all say' makes the cover story plainly about tonight, and 'the groom never woke up' is the English euphemism for a death that ties to s1e02's 'which one you don't wake up from'. l27 'died of shame' names a death without naming a method, as 'शर्म से गया' does. l28 is 'with your own hands' and not 'by your own hand', which in English suggests suicide. 'Whole sachet' matches the series' English anchor line 'Pour in the whole sachet.' l21 'latch' is कुंडी: the plain English word for the hasp the b8 insert shows torn out. l23 says 'dead' for 'नहीं रहा': 'gone' could be heard as 'left', and the cold viewer's question was exactly what Kiran knew.

l23 keeps 'Mausi' for the respect of आप, which English loses. l07 adds 'in there' because it is shouted through a door. l30 says 'any of us', not 'me', as the Hindi 'हम में से किसी को' does (D-007 direction 7: Mausi must not mark Kiran in front of Aditya as the one owed the news; the ledger's English default 'And you never told me?' is not used for that reason).

Emotion tags: every tag from the Hindi line is kept in the same position, including [quietly] on the new l29 and l30; no line needed a different cue. [hesitant] on l23 is in the verify-in-casting group; if the Kiran voice ignores it, S10 falls back to [quietly]. Gate 0b found [quietly] gave no measurable level change on v4, and the English takes for l01, l14 and l17 were already retaken with [calm] (voice/manifest.jsonl); if the Kiran voice whispers or ignores [quietly] on the new l14 or l30, S10 uses [calm] as those retakes did. If the Mausi voice ignores it on l27, read it as [calm], slower. l13 [calm], l29 [quietly], l14 [quietly]: no three quiet lines in a row from one voice, and none is whispered. The cliffhanger l28 is in the room, [calm], fully voiced, with the bed ducked under it.

Timing: targets for the unchanged lines are as before. Targets for the reworded and new lines are set at about 11 to 13 characters a second plus about 0.3 s per full stop inside the line, which sits between the old targets' basis and the cast's measured English rate on the existing takes (about 13 to 15 characters a second). Spoken targets 116.6 s; 16 speaker changes at 0.3 s add 4.8 s (l29 and l30 follow lines by the same speaker, so none is added); silences 24.3 s as in the Hindi; target_total_seconds 145.7. Measured English takes ran about 0.84 of their targets (84.2 s against 100.6 s), so the projection in clarity_pass (about 137 s) is the figure to use.

Length against the Hindi (skill rule: within about 15 per cent): the reworded and new lines are within 15 per cent of their Hindi targets except l23 (3.0 s against 3.6 s, about 17 per cent short) and l30 (2.8 s against 3.6 s, about 22 per cent short). Both are left short and not padded: they share b10 set-up 7, Kiran's single, with the 0.8 s hold after them, and Mausi's silence is the point of that shot. l06 stays about 18 per cent short, as before. l14, l16, l21 and l26 run longer than their old English lines because they carry the D-024 fixes; none is longer than its Hindi target.

Trim order (D-024 ruling 4; trigger: the measured English cut runs over 150 s): the silences only, the same as the Hindi: b2 3.0 to 2.0, b5a 2.5 to 1.5, b6 2.0 to 1.5, b7 5.5 to 4.5, b10 3.0 before l22 to 2.4. Every spoken line is a carrier of a viewer-ledger fact (s1b01.f01 to f11) or a locked or protected line, so no line is listed. If the cut is still over 150 s after the silences, it goes to the Arbiter. This replaces the earlier English trim order, which listed l25, l24, part of l21, and l05 with l06.

Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: Mausi (MAU-see), beta (BAY-taa, not the Greek letter), Damaad ji (da-MAAD jee), lakh (laakh, not 'lack'), Kiran (KI-run), Aditya (AA-dit-yaa), Mohit (MO-hit), Namaste (NUM-us-tay).

D-024 clarity pass (26 Nov), English. Mirrors script.hi.json's pass line for line. The previous English is kept unchanged as script.en.prev.json.
